paper.title_en: Multiple Phases in <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>Cr</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>As</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>: A Playground for Manipulating Topological Superconductivity
paper.abstract_en: Spin-triplet topological superconductors are rare but of fundamental interest as they can host Majorana bound states that can be used in fault-tolerant quantum computing. Recent efforts have been devoted to searching for spin-triplet states in U-based compounds, but these materials have a low transition temperature (<math display="inline"><msub><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub></math>) and coexisting competing orders, which creates significant experimental challenges and often leads to contradictory conclusions. The Cr-based candidate <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>Cr</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>As</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> offers a promising alternative: it has a much higher <math display="inline"><msub><mi>T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>6.2</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> and no magnetic order. Here we report a hallmark signature of spin-triplet superconductivity arising from the internal spin degrees of freedom via nuclear magnetic resonance measurements, and demonstrate the high tunability of the topological phases. We discovered three distinct superconducting phases and revealed the evolution of the paired-spins direction [<math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="bold">d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>-vector]. At low magnetic fields, <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>Cr</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>As</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> evolves from a helical (Phase A) to a chiral state (Phase B) with a rotation of the <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="bold">d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>-vector from in-plane to out-of-plane direction upon cooling, although both phases have point nodes in the gap. A line-nodal gap is realized in the high-field Phase C, where the <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="bold">d</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>-vector lies in the basal plane. These findings establish <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>Cr</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mi>As</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></math> as a model spin-triplet superconductor and a promising platform for manipulating topological phases.
